title: Class 9 Science RAG Chatbot
summary: A personal project: a RAG chatbot that helps Class 9 students with Science questions from NCERT textbook content, adapting answers to proficiency.
overview: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbot over NCERT Science PDFs. It retrieves relevant chunks from ChromaDB, generates answers with Azure OpenAI GPT-3.5, logs conversations in MongoDB and presents a Streamlit chat interface.
problem: Students need answers tied to their textbook and pitched at their level. Retrieval over the textbook content grounds the answers, and proficiency-aware prompts adjust the depth.
approach: Pre-processed PDFs are chunked and stored as embeddings in ChromaDB.
Semantic search retrieves relevant text chunks for each question.
Answers adapt to a student's proficiency level (Weak, Neutral, Strong).
The last 10 conversations from MongoDB are used for context-aware replies.
The Streamlit UI offers quick prompts, history and expandable retrieved content.

architecture.label: Retrieval
architecture.detail: ChromaDB vector search with Azure OpenAI embeddings over NCERT Science PDFs.

architecture.label: Generation
architecture.detail: Azure OpenAI GPT-3.5 produces proficiency-adapted answers.

architecture.label: Conversation memory
architecture.detail: MongoDB logs conversations; recent ones are added to the prompt.

architecture.label: Interface
architecture.detail: Streamlit chat UI.

workflow.step: Textbook PDFs are chunked and embedded into ChromaDB.

GPT-3.5 answers at the chosen proficiency level using the retrieved text and recent conversations.

title: AI Invoice & PDF Extraction

overview: A document-intelligence pipeline that turns unstructured invoice PDFs into structured data and classifies invoices. It combines Surya OCR for text recognition with a local Qwen2.5 model for language understanding, and falls back to the cloud-based OpenAI API when needed.
problem: Invoices arrive as PDFs with varying layouts, so the information inside them is unstructured. Downstream finance workflows need that information as structured fields and a classification, which plain text extraction alone does not provide.
approach: Built a hybrid OCR and LLM pipeline to extract structured information from invoice PDFs.
Integrated Surya OCR with a local Qwen2.5 model and a cloud-based OpenAI API fallback for document processing.
Implemented fallback logic between local and cloud LLMs to balance processing cost, latency, and extraction quality.
Designed the workflow to support structured data extraction and invoice classification from unstructured documents.

title: RAG-Based Chatbot Systems
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbots built on document ingestion, chunking, embeddings and vector search, plus a crypto research agent and a query-routing conversational agent.
overview: A body of work on RAG chatbots: ingesting documents, splitting them into chunks, embedding them, searching them by vector similarity and passing the retrieved content to an LLM so responses are grounded in relevant knowledge-base content. It also includes a crypto research agent that combines RAG with LSTM-based forecasting, and a conversational agent with query routing.
problem: A language model on its own does not know an organisation's documents and can produce unsupported answers. Retrieval gives the model relevant source material at question time so that responses can be grounded in it.
approach: Developed Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbots using document ingestion, text chunking, embeddings, and vector search.
Integrated retrieval pipelines with LLMs to generate responses grounded in relevant document or knowledge-base content.
Worked on a crypto research agent combining RAG with LSTM-based forecasting.
Developed a conversational agent with query-routing capabilities to support different types of user requests.
